machine: Mac M1 - 8-core CPU, 7-core GPU, 16 GB, macOS 26.6.2
methodology_warning: The mvp rows were measured over 48-frame runs, so scene construction (~60-90 s, a fixed cost independent of frame count) was swallowed into the per-frame figure and those numbers are badly pessimistic. The ep01 row is a steady-state measurement over 864 frames and is the one to use. Do not compare rows directly.

measurements.note: 1442 objects, 8 shots, 13 animation tracks, 180-degree motion blur
Phase-0 Short profile: 1080x1920 @ 8 spp on M1 CPU Cycles - the number the slate schedule turns on

findings: Metal was SLOWER than CPU on the M1. The 7-core GPU is weak and per-frame overhead dominates a simple scene. Do not assume the Mac's GPU is the fast path - measure it.
Scene construction is a fixed cost, so short benchmark runs overstate per-frame time badly. The 48-frame mvp figure was roughly half build time.
ep01 renders at 1.97 s/frame steady state - about half what the mvp benchmark implied, despite 2.6x the objects.

Run-to-run spread is real: the same 24-frame ad01/a01 bench measured 31.98 s/frame with other work on the same 8 cores and 26.86 s/frame on an idle machine - 19% apart. Run `harness bench` on an otherwise idle machine, and treat one row as a measurement with an error bar.

extrapolation.warning: Rebuilt on the steady-state ep01 figure, NOT the mvp figure.
extrapolation.assumed_scaling: linear in pixels and samples - optimistic, ignores VRAM pressure and the out-of-core fallback on a 10-12 GB card

control_passes.machine: Mac M1 - 8-core CPU, 7-core GPU, 16 GB, macOS 26.6.2
control_passes.why_it_matters: The generative interface renders control passes instead of a beauty plate, or alongside one. If the passes cost as much as the plate the loop is unaffordable and the architecture is pointless. They do not: depth is ~52x cheaper than the plate, and depth is the pass that carries the geometry.

findings: Depth costs about 2% of the beauty plate at the same resolution. The geometry-carrying pass is essentially free next to the pixels it replaces.
seg, edge and vis were measured at 320x180 only. The 1280x720 figures are UNKNOWN, and seg in particular is resolution-dependent.
Depth rendered through the AgX view transform spanned only 0.48-0.77 of its range. Standard is required, or the map is not a linear function of distance - see LESSONS.md 2026-09-18.
